The effect of this strong reconstruction on the band structure involves two ingredients: (1) the PMF and (2) variations of the local work function across the moiré plaquette35. We first calculated the band structure for the reconstructed AB and AA configurations, excluding the variations in work function (Fig. 5g,i). Two features emerge: (1) a substantial bandgap is opened owing to the reconstruction-induced difference between the on-site potential of each carbon sublattice35,36,37; (2) several fourfold spin-valley degenerate flat bands appear within the bandgap (Supplementary Information Sections 29, 31 and 32). Plotting the corresponding real-space wavefunctions (inset colour maps in Fig. 5g,i) reveals their localization at the vertices of the moiré domain AB-2, AA-1 and AA-2, in which strain and the PMF both peak. These flat bands can be interpreted as PLLs arising from the PMF. In reciprocal space, they are manifested as flat bands that host strongly localized electrons25. Equivalently, we can view them as strain-induced quantum dots situated at the moiré-domain vertices. Notably, because the zeroth PLL in graphene sits at the NP and is only half-filled, it cannot change the doping level unless its energy is shifted and hybridizes with either the valence or the conduction dispersive bands.

Taking into account the work-function landscape across the moiré plaquette (owing to local strain and van der Waals environment) shifts the flat bands away from the bandgap, hybridizing them with either the valence or the conduction bands and thus resulting in doping of graphene. The curvature at the AB-2 site lowers the hybridization of the pz orbital of carbons (similar to carbon nanotubes38), increases the local work function at AB-2 and consequently shifts its corresponding flat band downward (Fig. 5h). Conversely, the in-plane strain at AA-1 and AA-2 vertices reduces the carbon–carbon distance, resulting in the reduction of the local work function and upward shift of the corresponding flat bands39 (Fig. 5j). Other factors, such as the van der Waals environment, contribute with the same trend35,37 (Supplementary Information Section 27; Supplementary Figs. 43–45).

The resulting work-function variation lowers the flat bands towards the valence band in the AB configuration and raises them towards the conduction band in AA (Fig. 5h,j). Once the empty/filled flat bands in the AB/AA configuration cross the valence/conduction band, the holes/electrons trapped in the corresponding quantum dots are released into the body of the moiré domain and start to contribute to transport. This shifts the Fermi level away from the neutrality point to the valence/conduction bands and the AB/AA configuration will demonstrate p-doping/n-doping, respectively. In this picture, electrons are redistributed between the conductive moiré domain and the insulating quantum dots at its vertices.

Hole-side angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements corroborate this picture. Comparing the mhBN/graphene/hBN heterostructure against a conventional graphene/hBN reference region on the same flake (Fig. 5k,l), a flat band (orange) appears exclusively in the mhBN region and hybridizes with the neighbouring dispersive band (red), consistent with our above picture.

It has been revealed that such a doping mechanism explains the observed integer charging per moiré plaquette. In the simplest picture, each PLL holds g = gsgv = 4 states (spin × valley degeneracy). In the AB configuration (Fig. 5e), this condition is met at only one vertex per plaquette. Because the zero-energy PLL is initially half-filled, each vertex accommodates two more electrons (or holes), giving n/n0 = +2 for the initial p-doped state (blue sweep in Fig. 2d); in the AA configuration, two vertices contribute, giving n/n0 = −4 (red sweep). This accounts for the p-doping before the transition being consistently smaller than the n-doping after it.

According to recent reports, building on the above simplest picture, understanding such integer quantization also requires fundamental energy balance considerations. A well-established physical principle for structural stabilization seen in phenomena ranging from the Peierls transition in one-dimensional crystals to the filled shells of noble gases is as follows: when energy spectra are discrete, configurations with fully occupied and fully empty states separated by a gap become energetically favoured. In our system, the necessary discrete spectrum arises not from atomic orbitals or external magnetic fields but from PLLs generated by the strong periodic strain of the moiré reconstruction. Crucially, this solid-state system has a tunability absent in atomic prototypes: it can tune the electrostatic energy directly by solid gate and self-optimize the energy spectrum to maintain integer fillings. Similar to flux optimization in GaAs quantum rings40, the system can adjust the PMF strength (through strain redistribution) to ensure that the PLL degeneracy exactly matches the electron occupancy. The finite energy gain from fully occupying a Landau level compensates for the extra elastic deformation costs, effectively locking the system into a stable, integer-quantized state. We note that this self-optimization operates at the local scale involving only small strain variations around moiré vertices. This local self-optimization is distinct from the global structural transition itself, which is driven by the competition between van der Waals, elastic and electrostatic energies (Fig. 4).

Further evidence identifying commensurate filling of the discrete PLL spectrum as the origin of the integer doping, and ruling out alternative scenarios (charge trapping, Coulomb blockade of moiré-potential quantum dots, interfacial ferroelectricity and contact electrostatics), is provided in Supplementary Information Section 39.

In a recent development, we believe that our work opens a latest avenue for engineering structural and electronic phase transition in dynamical van der Waals systems through careful balancing of Coulomb, van der Waals and elastic energy contributions. Structures with several aligned interfaces can result in more complex phase transitions and electronic states. We also point out that the periodic arrangement of localized PLLs demonstrated here constitutes a regularly distributed array of quantum dots defined by strain. This connection to quantum dot physics opens avenues for further fundamental and applied investigations. Notably, such integer doping and phase transition occur across a broad range of moiré sizes (from 6 nm to 17.7 nm), eliminating the requirement for precise twist angle control in sample fabrication.

Heterostructures were assembled using the standard dry-transfer technique. Two device architectures were used: dual-gated hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN, in which the mhBN–hBN interface was intentionally misaligned by 15° to ensure superlubricity, and bottom-gated mhBN/graphene/hBN. Seven more types of reference device were fabricated by the same process (full list and data in Supplementary Information Section 4). The sample types are categorized by alignment and hBN thickness. The alignment scenarios include double alignment (a), single alignment (b), top and bottom hBN aligned with each other but not with the encapsulated graphene (c), single alignment with unencapsulated graphene (d) and a nonaligned three-layer stack (e). Samples with the same alignment are further subdivided by hBN thickness (bulk, bilayer and monolayer hBN), as illustrated in the schematics in Supplementary Fig. 7, into a1–a4, b1, b2, c1, d1 and e1. The a2 and a4 samples are the devices used in Fig. 2, listed in Supplementary Tables 1 (samples 1–8) and 2 (samples 9–10). Other sample types are for reference with data in Supplementary Information Section 4.

For the non-capped (single-gated) samples, simultaneous alignment of graphene to both hBN crystals was confirmed by AFM and transport measurements: the Fourier transform of the AFM topography (inset of Fig. 2b) shows two moiré periodicities of 10.8 nm and 12.0 nm (ref. 19), corroborated by the two sets of secondary Dirac points in the transfer curves13,14,15,41 (Fig. 2d). For the dual-gated encapsulated samples, in which the two moiré patterns are practically identical in size and the secondary Dirac points coincide in gate voltage, double alignment was confirmed primarily by Raman spectroscopy combined with optical imaging and AFM (ref. 42). Detailed analysis is given in Supplementary Information Section 2. The thickness of the hBN layers (down to monolayer) was confirmed by Raman and AFM measurements (Supplementary Information Section 2).

Industry observers note that transport measurements were performed in a TeslatronPT cryostat at a base temperature of T = 1.6 K, equipped with a superconducting magnet providing fields up to 14 T. Longitudinal and Hall resistances were measured in a four-terminal configuration using standard low-frequency lock-in SR860 lock-in amplifiers, with an AC excitation current of 5 nA at 37 Hz to avoid sample heating. Gate voltages were applied by a Keithley 2601 source meter. For dual-gated devices, the top-gate and back-gate voltages were swept simultaneously along the D = 0 line30 unless stated otherwise. The critical transition voltage is independent of the gate sweep rate (Supplementary Information Section 15); control experiments excluding contamination and other artefacts are detailed in Supplementary Information Sections 5 and 14.

The stability, work function, electronic structures and charge transfer of the hBN/graphene/hBN heterostructures have been thoroughly studied using DFT calculations. Our calculations are based on the Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof functional as implemented in the Vienna Ab Initio Simulation Package (VASP). The interaction between the valence electrons and ionic cores is described within the projector augmented-wave approach with a plane-wave energy cut-off of 500 eV. The widely used semi-local approximations for the exchange-correlation energy do not take long-range correlations into account correctly. Thus, they fail to reproduce van der Waals attraction and the prediction of equilibrium geometries of van der Waals bound layered systems. To address the concern, the dispersion correction schemes proposed by Grimme were used to treat the interlayer interaction between graphene and hBN layers. The Brillouin zone was sampled with the Monkhorst–Pack grid and the grid sizes depend on the size of the supercells used. The grid was chosen to be as dense as 31 × 31 × 1 for a primitive cell and Γ-point only for a large supercell of near 5 nm. The vacuum space of at least 15 Å was used to avoid interaction between neighbouring layers. In the structural energy minimization, the atomic coordinates are allowed to relax until the forces on all of the atoms are less than 0.01 eV Å−1. The energy tolerance is 10−6 eV.

Because full-scale DFT calculation would be computationally unrealistic for a moiré unit cell consisting of 56 × 56 atoms of graphene monolayer and at least twice the 55 × 55 atoms of two hBN layers, we would investigate the structure using a combination of DFT calculations and empirical potentials MD simulations. For specified stacking of the hBN/graphene/hBN heterostructures, calculations were done using the commensurate structure with the graphene lattice. To understand the adhesion energy and the work function distribution of the moiré structure, we screen the local stacking of the moiré cell of hBN/graphene/hBN using a 21 × 21 grid of sampling points. The structure at each sampling point was obtained by shifting the graphene with respect to the hBN layers on the two sides. To model the gate-induced electron doping in graphene, extra electrons were added to the supercell and a uniform positive charge background was added to compensate and ensure the charge neutrality of the system.

Sources indicate that the structure relaxations were implemented in the Large-scale Atomic/Molecular Massively Parallel Simulator (LAMMPS). We used many-body Tersoff potentials to treat the in-plane C–C and B–N interactions. The interlayer van der Waals interaction between the graphene and hBN was described by the registry-dependent Kolmogorov–Crespi potential. To model the interlayer interaction between graphene and hBN under gating, we vary the strength of the C–B interaction relative to the C–N interaction using a scaling parameter (s). We found that, for s = 5% and s = 50%, the potential is qualitatively consistent with the DFT interlayer adhesion of the trilayer heterostructure in the absence and presence of doping, respectively. Using the s = 50% scaling of the C–B/C–N interaction, we successfully simulated the structural transition of the heterostructure. To include the substrate effect of bulk hBN and model the interlayer interactions among different boron nitride layers, we proposed a Lennard–Jones 6–12 potential to describe the repulsive and attractive terms, and Coulomb’s law is used for the electrostatic interactions. This yields.

in which ϵij and σij are the potential parameters to control the strength of the attractive and repulsive interactions, respectively, rij is the interaction distance between atom i and atom j, qi and qj are the atomic partial charge in units of the elementary charge and Kc is the coulombic constant. We set 0.2 and −0.2 for the B and N, respectively after careful evaluation. Because of the smaller van der Waals radius of B (about 1.92 Å) and large interlayer distance of hBN layers (about 3.30 Å), we neglected the short-range B–B interactions in this study. ϵBN and ϵNN were set to 0.3035 and 10.8237 meV, respectively. Also, we used 3.75 and 3.1461 Å for σBN and σNN, respectively. During the simulation, the cut-off distance was set to 8 Å for the attractive and repulsive terms. A long-range solver of the standard coulombic Ewald summations was used to compute long-range coulombic interactions or long-range interactions. The atomic structures were equilibrated using the NVT ensemble (canonical ensemble). A 2.0-ns annealing process from 300 K to 1 K was first carried out and then the other 0.5-ns timescale was implemented to stabilize the structures. A time step of 1.0 fs was used and the relaxation was completed when the forces are less than 10−6 eV Å−1. The unrotated heterostructures were modelled by 56 × 56 unit cells of graphene and 55 × 55 unit cells of hBN, resulting in a 1.8% mismatch in lattice constant. We used four monolayers of hBN to imitate bulk substrate, in which the bottom two layers were fixed and the top two layers allowed relaxation during the MD simulations.

It has been revealed that the lattice structures of graphene and hBN are incommensurate; although both feature a honeycomb lattice (graphene of carbon atoms and hBN of boron and nitrogen atoms), the hBN lattice period is δ ≈ 1.8%, longer than that of graphene, a = 0.246 nm. Including an anticlockwise twist of the hBN layer, θ, the interference of the two lattice potentials at the interface gives a moiré superlattice, magnified from the graphene lattice, with moiré superlattice period \(\lambda \approx a/\sqrt{{\delta }^{2}+{\theta }^{2}}\), and rotated by φ ≈ −arctan(θ/δ). The moiré superlattice Bragg vectors are constructed as linear combinations of the ‘first star’ of non-zero vectors, Gm ≈ δ · gm − θ(ez × gm) m = (0, 1,…, 5), expressed in terms of the first star of graphene vectors, \({{\bf{g}}}_{{\rm{m}}}=\frac{4\pi }{\sqrt{3}a}\left(-\sin \frac{m2\pi }{3},\cos \frac{m2\pi }{3}\right)\), and depicted alongside the moiré Brillouin zone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 10:25 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 11:32 EST, 20 November 2026.

Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada insists the team got 'fundamentally better' after this summer's transfer window, as he warned ‘spending just for the sake of it’ is not the route to putting United back on top.

In his first sit-down interview in five months, Berrada tackled topics ranging from the relationship between the Glazers and Ineos, the imminent departure of youngster JJ Gabriel, the decision not to sign a left back in the summer, as well as the decision to push ahead for a fresh stadium despite supporter backlash on matchdays.

The United chief has been at the centre of furious protests and anti-ownership chanting at matches this season, alongside Director of Football Jason Wilcox, and he accepted that criticism of United's leadership has, mostly, been fair.

In an interview that aired shortly after latest head coach Mauricio Pochettino spoke to the media for the first time, Berrada was pressed on how much accountability falls at his door with United heading to Anfield this weekend 18th in the Premier League table.

'I think if you think about the fact we've had three permanent managers in less than three seasons, clearly we haven't achieved the stability that we wanted, that's for sure,' Berrada told Sky Sports.

'When it doesn't work out with the coach or the manager, we are all responsible. Myself, the football leadership, everyone who is involved around the coach and the staff and the players. We have to continue improving and getting better.

Manchester United's CEO Omar Berrada finally fronted up in an interview with Sky Sports.

Michael Carrick's sacking was yet another managerial change at United, with the hierarchy under massive scrutiny and Mauricio Pochettino now in the hotseat.

'There are different circumstances why it didn't work out with Erik [ten Hag], and Ruben [Amorim], and now Michael [Carrick], and we are always learning and, as I said, trying to improve and understand what has failed.

'The challenge is we're trying to find the right manager for the squad that we have with a specific set of skills in that moment to make them perform at their best level.

Sources indicate that 'It's true, we have to accept the criticism that we haven't been able to achieve that stability with one coach and our aim is to do that as soon as possible. Of course, we hope now that Mauricio coming in will give us that stability that I think we all need.'.

Berrada's links to Manchester City, where he worked prior to joining United, were brought up, not least given he worked at the club during the period that City have had charges brought against them.

'I'm not concerned,' Berrada insisted.

But at his upcoming home there are challenges aplenty, not least having got another managerial appointment wrong, sacking Carrick less than six months after handing him a two-year deal, and so it was put to Berrada: is the club actually progressing?

'It's not good enough, not acceptable and that's why we've made the change that we made so that we can move forward,' he concluded.

(L-R) Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Berrada and Jason Wilcox have drawn plenty of ire from Man United fans.

Sources indicate that 'But we are laying the foundations for sustained growth, to put us in a position where we can be competitive consistently. It's not always been that.

Recent findings suggest that 'Last year we finished third, we were happy with the squad, we were happy with the way we were going. And now, a few months later, we are not where we need to be. But the foundations are there and I am convinced that we are heading in the right direction. Very positive.'.

  • FIORENTINA (4-2-3-1) Frey; De Silvestri (86' Comotto), Dainelli, Kroldrup, Gobbi; Montolivo, Zanetti (80' Jorgensen); Marchionni, Santana, Vargas; Gilardino Allenatore: Prandelli.

Il 24 novembre 2009, allo stadio Artemio Franchi, la Fiorentina affronta l'Olympique Lione nella penultima giornata della fase a gironi di Champions League. I viola devono fare i conti con le assenze di Mutu, Gamberini e Natali, mentre Jovetic, recuperato in extremis, parte dalla panchina. Di fronte c'è una squadra già qualificata e saldamente al comando del girone. A Firenze, invece, si sognano gli ottavi di finale che mancano da dieci anni. C'è anche un tabù da sfatare: nei tre precedenti confronti con i francesi, la Fiorentina non è mai riuscita a conquistare una vittoria. Il successo ottenuto all'andata contro il Liverpool, però, ha messo la squadra di Prandelli in una posizione favorevole, con cinque punti di vantaggio sugli inglesi.

La serata si decide al 28', quando l'arbitro Benquerenca concede un calcio di rigore per un fallo di Cissokho su Marchionni. Dal dischetto si presenta Vargas, che non sbaglia e porta in vantaggio i viola. Una rete che premia una Fiorentina già pericolosa in precedenza, con Santana e Gilardino fermati dai legni e Lloris protagonista di un intervento prodigioso. Nel finale è Frey a salire in cattedra, respingendo gli ultimi tentativi del Lione e blindando una vittoria fondamentale. Al triplice fischio, il Franchi può festeggiare: la Fiorentina è agli ottavi di finale di Champions League.

FIORENTINA (4-2-3-1) Frey; De Silvestri (86' Comotto), Dainelli, Kroldrup, Gobbi; Montolivo, Zanetti (80' Jorgensen); Marchionni, Santana, Vargas; Gilardino Allenatore: Prandelli.

LIONE (4-3-3) Lloris; Gassama, Cris, Boumsong, Cissokho; Pjanic, Makoun, Kallstrom; Govou (74' Delgado), Gomis (79' Ederson), Bastos (67' Lisandro Lopez Allenatore: Puel.

#152940. VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

📅 05 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 18m • 📚 Deep Dive (3604 w)

VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

📅 05 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3604 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?
  • Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.
  • Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

The big moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Industry observers note that replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

On this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams said: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”.

According to recent reports, glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” said Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision. We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”.

Industry observers note that while Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

Recent findings suggest that the grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

Recent findings suggest that one of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi said: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something important.

“If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with big qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi noted: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”.

Recent findings suggest that after the disallowed Williams goal, Forest were feeling further aggrieved soon after when Rodrigo Bentancur appeared to pull back substitute Igor Jesus in the penalty area. These are two teams clearly in period of transition and patience will be required from both sets of supporters.

Mohammed Kudus comes on for Sávio and Andy Robertson for Destiny Udogie.

Tyrick Mitchell has scored his second. What do they say about London buses….

Mitchell rampaging up the left, shoots. It’s blocked by García who tries to clear by hitting it straight into Mitchell’s foot whence it ricochets past Bernd Leno.

The substantial headline news from Tottenham is that Mykhailo Mudryk is on the bench.

Signed from Chelsea on deadline day on an initial loan, Mudryk was once branded as a future Ballon d’Or winner by Roberto De Zerbi after they worked together at Shakhtar.

Mudryk has not played a competitive match since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

Will this be third time lucky for Tottenham Hotspur after their £300m+ summer reset?

In typical Tottenham fashion, their start to the Premier League season has not been straightforward with two defeats, five goals conceded and none scored so far.

The popular opinion is that it will eventually click, but Tottenham’s supporters are still scarred by those two successive 17th-placed finishes.

Forest have won their last four games against Spurs, so it will be an early sign of promise if Roberto De Zerbi can secure a positive result here.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

Recent findings suggest that “I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca noted, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more key to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just stated he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

Recent findings suggest that “I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very vital that he is with us.”.

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

Industry observers note that we have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi plans to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

Palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.

Ma Kolo Muani chi l'ha voluto alla Juventus? Spalletti fa il Conte per evitare che finisca come all'Inter: uno scambio gli toglierebbe ogni alibi

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (626 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tuttomercatoweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that la Juventus in estate ha speso 41 milioni di euro più dodici di bonus per acquistare a titolo definitivo Randal Kolo Muani.
  • Nessuno è adatto: "Abbiamo bisogno di un centravanti perché non l'abbiamo comprato.
  • It has been revealed that ma allora chi ha avallato l'acquisto di Kolo Muani e degli altri centravanti?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that la Juventus in estate ha speso 41 milioni di euro più dodici di bonus per acquistare a titolo definitivo Randal Kolo Muani. Ha definito l'operazione dopo una telenovela durata oltre un anno, dopo aver già testato il calciatore a Torino nella stagione 2024/25. Non solo: sempre la scorsa estate in una campagna trasferimenti da oltre 120 milioni di acquisti ne ha investiti 16 per acquistare Jeff Ekhator del Genoa e circa tre per il prestito di Nick Woltemade. La società bianconera ha definito queste tre operazioni con l'intenzione di mettere a disposizione di Luciano Spalletti un nuovo centravanti, l'ha fatto perché Jonathan David - altro numero 9 - non era ritenuto adatto alla Juventus del manager di Certaldo. E non lo era nemmeno Lois Openda. L'unico centravanti 'giusto' per Spalletti era Dusan Vlahovic, calciatore volato a Istanbul perché alla Juve voleva guadagnare più di tutti gli altri nonostante un rendimento non all'altezza degli 80 milioni spesi. Che al Besiktas guadagna 8 milioni più bonus dopo aver incassato un bonus alla firma da dieci milioni di euro.

E gli altri? E gli ultimi tre arrivati? Nessuno è adatto: "Abbiamo bisogno di un centravanti perché non l'abbiamo comprato. Kolo Muani lo rimetterò lì perché serve qualcuno che giochi in quella posizione: nel calcio d'oggi serve una punta fisica che sappia giocare spalle alla porta. Poi è inutile parlare di Spalletti via. C'è bisogno di gente fisica, che riceva la pallata addosso e sappia giocare con le mani addosso del centrale avversario. Ora è così. Si vince i duelli. Ci vuole gente fisica che vinca i duelli ed esca dalle mini prigioni che ci sono in campo", le parole di Spalletti dopo la larga vittoria contro il Venezia.

It has been revealed that ma allora chi ha avallato l'acquisto di Kolo Muani e degli altri centravanti? E' possibile che la Juventus abbia speso metà del suo budget estivo per tre centravanti che non erano graditi al suo allenatore? Evidentemente no, anche perché in estate la società bianconera faceva sapere di definire tutte le operazioni dopo un confronto con l'allenatore. E lo stesso Spalletti - dopo aver fatto cadere dalla torre Damien Comolli - esprimeva soddisfazione per il lavoro portato avanti braccio a braccio col nuovo amministratore delegato Giovanni Carnevali.

E allora cosa c'è dietro? Cosa sta succedendo? La verità è che le parole di Antonio Conte non hanno scosso solo l'ambiente bianconero, ma anche lo stesso tecnico di Certaldo che ha il timore con questa stagione di preparare il terreno al manager leccese proprio come fece all'Inter. Che sabato pomeriggio ha replicato così alla bussata dell'allenatore leccese alla porta bianconera: "Io quando non allenavo studiavo gli altri tecnici con rispetto". Un titolo che non è passato inosservato, una conferenza stampa a cui ne ha fatto seguito un'altra in cui Spalletti - proprio come avrebbe fatto Conte - ha esplicitamente chiesto un acquisto per gennaio. Un altro innesto dopo i 9-10 acquisti estivi.

Recent findings suggest that la Juventus in questa situazione è pronta ad assecondare il suo allenatore, l'alternativa sarebbe quella di cambiare guida tecnica e non è questa oggi la strada che vuole seguire la società. Non facile però nella prossima finestra di calciomercato trovare un centravanti all'altezza della Juventus. Le alternative al momento sono principalmente due: o investire una quarantina di milioni per quel Varela che sta facendo sfracelli a Monza ma ha solo poche settimane in Serie A. Oppure - e questa è l'ipotesi più probabile - portare avanti la trattativa con l'Atletico Madrid per cedere Jonathan David a titolo definitivo ai colchoneros e far fare il viaggio opposto a quell'Alexander Sorloth che dall'alto dei suoi 196 centimetri il centravanti di lotta e di governo lo sa fare benissimo.

Published: 11:37 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 11:44 EST, 20 November 2026.

Sources indicate that derek McInnes can be understood in wanting a quiet January window. He’s still bonding a squad of players together. Drama and diversions are the last thing he needs when there looks to be an opportunity to win a title on the horizon.

In the case of Olwethu Makhanya, for example, this is definitely not the time to sell.

The 22-year-old South African has been impressive at centre-back, but it will take a campaign catching the attention in high-level European football for him to raise his value to Calvin Bassey levels and beyond.

Same goes for the likes of Ryan Naderi. Getting into the Czechia squad and increasing his range of experience makes him a more interesting prospect, but UEFA competition is a platform that ought to increase his premium.

McInnes, as he did this week, has to say he wants to keep his more prominent talents anyway. It would be strange to appear accepting of the board cashing in on bigger players.

When it comes to Nico Raskin, however, things are different. A buyer for him should have been found in the summer after his World Cup involvement with Belgium.

Rangers midfielder Nico Raskin is an asset who could be sold in the January transfer window.

From the chit-chat around the game, it does not seem unreasonable to think Rangers maybe overvalued him in the initial part of that window and missed the boat in terms of securing a sale.

If he stays for the rest of this season and enters the final year of his contract, though, the money you can ask for naturally reduces. The club might seek to tie him up on a upcoming deal, of course, but his remarks about being ‘mentally ready to leave’ at the start of the season point to the most likely direction of travel.

According to recent reports, is he irreplaceable? Not at all. And this is where forward planning should come into the mix.

If there’s someone out there willing to edge anywhere close to the £15m mark for the 25-year-old, they should be getting sounded out now – with a contingency plan being discussed and worked on in tandem.

Yes, Rangers need to get back to winning silverware, but the need to start raising funds through selling players – and replacing them - at appropriate times is pressing too.

As often remarked here, they can’t keep spending money the way they have been without considerably more coming back in return.

It has been revealed that raskin’s a good player, but his three-and-a-half years at Ibrox have hardly been shaped by his propensity for winning medals, have they? If a realistic fee is there in January, there’s a case to make for it being taken.

Mario Aiello, direttore sportivo dell'Avellino, è stato intervistato da Radio Kiss Kiss.

Recent findings suggest that “La Serie B è un campionato difficilissimo dove dalla prima all'ultima sono tutti attrezzati. Ci sono risultati sorprendenti. Noi per fortuna siamo riusciti ad avere un certo andamento equilibrato, abbiamo fatto qualche risultato importante e stiamo cercando di crescere partita dopo partita per consolidare questa categoria”.

Recent findings suggest that “I tifosi hanno sempre diritto e dovere di poter sognare perché nel calcio non si può mai sapere. Noi che chiaramente ci operiamo all'interno abbiamo invece il dovere di essere sempre equilibrati e di cercare di fare i passi uno alla volta cercando di consolidare questo club, sia dal punto di vista tecnico, sia a livello di tutte quelle che sono le strutture che possono far crescere il nostro valore. Nel calcio tutto può succedere, sicuramente dobbiamo andare avanti mantenendo sempre un profilo basso ma cercando di pensare in grande".

Sources indicate that "Lui ha sempre avuto talento, qualità e forza. Chiaramente come tutti i giovani hanno avuto bisogno di tempo per maturare sotto tanti aspetti sotto il profilo tattico e caratteriale. Ora lui è più andato avanti, è più acquisito consapevolezza dei propri mezzi e adesso probabilmente è uno dei calciatori che in Serie B fa più la differenza e secondo me ha i numeri, la forza, il motore e la qualità per poter essere protagonista anche in Serie A".

“La società non si tira indietro, però riteniamo di avere una squadra abbastanza completa e quindi se in questa fase stiamo semplicemente monitorando quello che può essere il meglio in termini prospettici anche per il nostro club. Se qualcuno dovesse chiedere di andare via o per scarso utilizzo o per altri motivi noi sicuramente ci possiamo far trovare pronti e poi vediamo un attimino qual è l'eventuale opportunità da cogliere”. Le sue parole riportate da Pianetaserieb.it.

Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions

📅 06 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 33 min read (6613 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~33 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.
  • Sources indicate that the chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead.
  • That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

Sources indicate that the chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

Morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm.

Instead, Arteta’s players drove this contest, and the sequence of chances that came and went was dizzying at times. Their best players scored the two goals. First Kai Havertz, who now has three in four games this season, and then the captain Martin Ødegaard who dispatched what would be the winner.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck.

Ødegaard looked like the veteran of a title-winning season, and a deep run in the World Cup – an accomplished, shrewd performer in a midfield that was fought over ferociously all afternoon.

As for the game’s defining moment – it would be hard to overlook the feint from Havertz for the winning goal. It deceived the Chelsea players around him and created the channel for Christos Tzolis’s cross to reach Ødegaard. His goal was a close copy, in style and personnel, of the one he scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield but it was crowned by Havertz’s bluff. He shaped to take the ball and let it run under his foot at the last moment.

According to recent reports, this was Chelsea’s first defeat in three – leaving only Arsenal and City with nine points from their first three games – although the seven goals conceded is the standout. For all the jet fuel in their attack they keep conceding. This was a much more exacting test than Fulham and Brighton previously, but even so. Alonso has introduced his preferred back three, often a back five, and it is a work in progress.

It has been revealed that arsenal have set the standard in that regard and they were uncompromising again. They did not replicate the errors that led to the Rogers goal and they pushed the limits at all times. Gabriel Magalhães kicked Emi Martínez in the head competing for a ball in the Chelsea area. Myles Lewis-Skelly went after João Pedro. Ben White and Roméo Lavia saw things differently in the first half. This Arsenal team does not shy away from those confrontations in the way their predecessors often did.

In fact, it was notable just how furiously Rogers reacted to Declan Rice when the two England team-mates converged as the Chelsea man charged off to join a late counter-attack. The bad feeling lingered even after the game when Rogers seemed unwilling to forgive. Rice had applied the minimum contact and the maximum cynicism to stop Rogers while the attention of referee Chris Kavanagh was elsewhere.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh.

All that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be noted that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a big summer acquisition. Viktor Gyökeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

“Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’s right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

According to recent reports, arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup-winning substitutes – Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

It has been revealed that in the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

Recent findings suggest that for the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Ødegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN.

Chelsea had profited from the quick ball out to their right where Calafiori was often out of position in the left-back slot and Pedro Neto could cut in on his left foot. That seemed to be the sacrifice that Arteta was prepared to make in keeping the hammer on Chelsea. If Neto had not struck the post in one such escape in time added on at the end of the first half it might have been different.

Sources indicate that ødegaard struck what would be the winner early in the first half, and although Chelsea fizzed enough in the later stages it always felt as though it was Arsenal’s game. Raya came into his own in the 89th minute when Estêvão, a substitute, cut in from the right and hit a fierce shot that the goalkeeper pushed over. It was close in some ways – and in others not at all.

According to recent reports, “It hurts. It hurts because a defeat has to hurt. It has been a very intense game with different moments for everything. We had chances to equalise. In the first half as well a couple of chances. Never happy if you lose.

According to recent reports, “After we scored, there were 15-20 minutes where we had to defend too much and we were struggling a bit to get control. We then had better spells with the ball. Overall, it was a very tight, very intense game. We could do better with the second goal to conceded too early. The guys gave everything, tried everything. It has to hurt.

“It is about preparing the best possible way to compete the best possible way. You need to control the overloads on the right side. It is part of the game to have these actions. We continue. It is game three and this is going to be a long, long ride.”.

"That's not sustainable" Daniel Sturridge reflects Chelsea's performance after the 2-1 defeat to Arsenal 💭 pic.twitter.com/3EMx88QLA0.

"He's not the goalkeeper that won the World Cup" 🏆Jamie Carragher states Emi Martinez is not as quick or sharp as he once was 🧤 pic.twitter.com/SOp4XhoYIr.

Industry observers note that “I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that [William] Saliba, who is genuinely world-class arguably, probably the best centre-back in world football, has not played a minute of football so far this season. And it does not look like anyone can score against them.

Sources indicate that “There is a massive gulf between both teams; their XIs and the squads. It will take Chelsea a while to get to that level, if they can get there. But I thought Arsenal were fantastic today. We do not normally see Arsenal in these games, end-to-end, because they very rarely go behind. They are so strong defensively they do not need to get involved in those games.

“They still did not look like they were going to give too much away, even though they were bombing forwards and putting so many bodies in the opposition box.”.

Industry observers note that “It was a massive game with a tough opponent. It was really hard for us; we got there in the end. Our mentality is to keep fighting. Conceding early was not ideal but we reacted really well. We played well in the second half and got our reward. We revealed our quality today. The result reflected that.”.

On his relationship with Kai Havertz:.

It has been revealed that “He is a really smart player and moves so well. He takes defenders attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind I am always free. It was a brilliant goal.”.

Industry observers note that “We knew Arsenal were the better team and they have proven that in this game. The question before today was, how close are Chelsea? And [Xabi] Alonso will be proud of what he has seen. There are obviously improvements to be made, but they gave it a right good go. A lot of very good things and they will be frustrated and disappointed, but they may potentially look back on this game as a good moment rather than as bad as it may feel right now.”.

Fofana brings down Havertz with a rather silly challenge and Arsenal have a free-kick out on the right, with the chance to send it into the Chelsea box. Odegaard drills it low in towards the near post and picks out the run of Calafiori. The Italian’s effort is saved by Martinez’s legs and then a mad scramble for the ball ensues. It is difficult to see where the ball is and ends up going out for a goal kick. Martinez stays down and is receiving treatment to his head. It comes as a result of Gabriel’s boot flying into Martinez’s head. Should VAR be taking a look at that one? They clear it but Gabriel might count himself lucky that a review for violent conduct was not called.

Not even two minutes into the game, Chelsea take the lead and it is a man Arsenal wanted over the summer who scores against them. Rogers, on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area, watches the ball onto his foot and volleys first time into the bottom left corner. A fine finish from Rogers and Chelsea have the perfect start. How will Arsenal respond?

Morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm.

The first goal Arsenal concede this season is scored by the first player they wanted to sign in the summer.

Wow. That had echoes of Eze scoring against Tottenham last season. Just as Spurs had missed out to Arsenal for Eze, Arsenal missed out to Chelsea for Rogers. So what happens? Of course, he scores. After just two minutes. I’m also pretty sure Rogers imitated the Thierry Henry celebration next to the corner flag just to rub salt into Arsenal’s wounds.

The two bosses, who have known each other since they were children, share a warm embrace before kick-off.

We are under way at the Emirates. Both sides have 100% records coming into this one but at least one of those will fall today.

Perhaps some early mind games from Arsenal as Chelsea were left waiting in the tunnel for a little while before Arsenal eventually emerged. Eventually both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this afternoon:.

It has been revealed that it is a relationship that Arteta has previously described as “deeper than just a friendship”. It started with skateboards and sand, as they made the daily journey to the beach to play tennis and football, and continued into their adult lives. When Alonso was playing for Liverpool and Arteta for Everton, there was a time when they both had flats on the fourth floor of the same building in the Albert Dock.

Industry observers note that it is extraordinary that these two individuals – born just a few months apart – now find themselves in positions of such significance in English football. But it is not a coincidence. Throughout their lives, they have driven each other forward.

In a recent development, “This kid, he was maybe even crazier than me about football,” Alonso once stated of Arteta and their shared childhood. “He was a little bit younger than me and my friends – just a few months maybe. A personal opinion that no one asked for: Arsenal should have signed Joao Pedro last summer, when the Brazilian joined Chelsea for £60m. Arsenal bought Viktor Gyokeres instead, in a deal that could ultimately be more expensive, and there is no doubt which forward offers more to their team. Joao Pedro always seemed to cause problems for Arsenal’s defence when he played against them during his time at Brighton, and he has a flexibility and versatility that would have been perfect for Arteta’s system. Arsenal had twice explored the possibility of signing him over the years. It is surely a source of regret that they never became serious about it. So far this season, Joao Pedro has scored and assisted in both league games. Gyokeres, by contrast, has played zero minutes.

It has been revealed that mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are “better equipped” for success this season, despite falling short in their attempts to add a top-class attacker. Arsenal have allowed four forward players to leave this summer and brought in one, Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

Industry observers note that the departures of Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri (on loan) have raised concerns among supporters that the champions lack firepower. Moves for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez did not come to fruition. Arteta, though, feels Arsenal are stronger now than at the end of last season following a summer in which they added midfielder Bruno Guimarães and defender Ezri Konsa.

According to recent reports, “We are better equipped,” remarked Arteta, who faces Rogers and close friend Xabi Alonso. “We have more players available than the start of last season. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership, which is very vital.”.

Asked specifically about the attack, he added: “Yeah, but that’s another question. We have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not. Let’s see. We need to play. I don’t like to make assumptions.

“It’s not just the responsibility of those players, it’s the team and the dynamic. We have multiple options to play there with different profiles. It’s human nature. When you talk to people and you ask: ‘Ok, what is on your bucket list?’ Sometimes we forget the reverse bucket list, which are the things you already have that are incredible. It’s very notable to value what we have, what we have created together. The ambition is great, but [don’t] lose perspective to what we already have which is amazing.”.

Two sides with 100% records meet in a London derby in north London as defending champions Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates. Arsenal have wins over Coventry and Aston Villa to their name whilst Chelsea have beaten Fulham and Brighton.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal could make it three wins from three to start the season, a feat they have only achieved once in the last 21 seasons. They have lost just one of their last 29 Premier League London derbies. Mikel Arteta comes up against his childhood friend Xabi Alonso today.

“Really happy for him [Alonso],” Arteta said. “It is incredible because obviously we have the history we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola]. To be facing each other at such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience. Now it will be tougher to meet because of the schedule we both have but that friendship will go for many years. We shared some great moments but now it is the competition and when you face each other, you know what happens.”.

According to recent reports, chelsea were involved in late drama on transfer deadline day. They were on the verge of signing midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco only to see that deal fall through at the last minute. After being linked with a move away throughout the summer, Chelsea did in the end sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint Premier League transfer record fee of £125m.

In a recent development, “In football, many things happen and you need to be prepared for everything,” Chelsea boss Alonso mentioned. “With Enzo, we have had conversations, but always with respect for what he has done for the club. It has been great, we are thankful, but it is time to move forward. We take all the decisions together. We are responsible for them, we work together with every decision, big and small.

“We knew that, ultimately, the last goal is to have the best for the team, the best for the squad, the best for daily work here. We want to build a good spirit, a good team, and we have always taken decisions thinking we want to reach that. We have the squad we have. We have a lot of massive personalities, players with a lot of quality in all the different positions, different lines and now we are ready to go.”.

Arsenal won this fixture 2-1 last season, with William Saliba and Jurrien Timber earning Mikel Arteta’s side three points on their way to the title. Arsenal are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League matches against Chelsea.

Team news from the Emirates to follow shortly.

TransA-MERFISH reveals divergent post-retinal direction-selective circuits

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 103 min read (20574 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~103 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A major goal in neuroscience is to map the transformation of information as it flows through the brain.
  • Sources indicate that A central objective in neuroscience is to characterize the computational transformations that occur across successive nodes of neural circuits.
  • According to recent reports, efforts to map neural circuits have yielded a diverse array of methodologies, yet existing ‘gold-standard’ approaches face considerable scalability and molecular identification constraints.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A major goal in neuroscience is to map the transformation of information as it flows through the brain. For example, neurons at many levels of the visual hierarchy are attuned to motion direction1,2,3,4,5. However, links between motion-selective computations and cell types at various stages of the visual hierarchy remain unidentified. A key first step in delineating these relationships is to map the wiring diagrams that connect different motion-selective cell types. Here we establish a systematic, cell-type-specific circuit-mapping method, combining an anterograde trans-neuronal fluorescent tracer (mWGA–mCherry)6 with spatial transcriptomics (multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (MERFISH))7,8 to establish TransA-MERFISH. We used TransA-MERFISH to comprehensively map the synaptic target cell types of four retinal ganglion cell subclasses in superior colliculus (SC) at cell-type resolution. These experiments unexpectedly revealed that retinal on–off direction-selective ganglion cells (ooDSGCs) innervate several direction-selective SC cell types, but do not innervate a SC cell type that was previously reported to display strong direction-selective responses. We validated these results using orthogonal approaches and demonstrated the sensitivity and specificity of TransA-MERFISH. Functional studies of SC activity before and after ablation of retinal direction-selective circuits confirmed that these computationally distinct, ooDSGC-dependent and -independent direction-selective cell types are commingled in SC. Together, our study establishes TransA-MERFISH as a robust framework for mapping wiring diagrams at the cell-type level and uncovers divergent computational mechanisms of motion detection in early visual processing.

Sources indicate that A central objective in neuroscience is to characterize the computational transformations that occur across successive nodes of neural circuits. In the visual system, this requires defining the mechanisms by which retinal signals are integrated and processed as they ascend to higher brain centres. Among these, motion signals are particularly salient, providing the sensory substrate for critical behaviours such as predatory pursuit, escape and spatial navigation9,10. Over the past half-century, neurons in various brain areas have been found to respond to visual motion. A particularly common form of motion sensitivity is a preference for stimuli moving in a certain direction, a property known as direction selectivity that is observed in the retina, SC and cortex1,2,3,4,5. However, relationships between direction-selective cell types in different brain areas are unknown, leaving equally unclear how direction-selective activity is used and transformed across different stages of the visual hierarchy. A key obstacle has been the lack of a wiring diagram to guide understanding of information flow between the tens of different retinal ganglion cell (RGC) types and similarly diverse neuronal cell types in target areas such as SC. Here, we describe the development of a technological platform that enabled us to address these knowledge gaps.

According to recent reports, efforts to map neural circuits have yielded a diverse array of methodologies, yet existing ‘gold-standard’ approaches face considerable scalability and molecular identification constraints. Although electron microscopy provides high-resolution reconstructions11,12,13,14, it remains incompatible with the molecular profiling of pre- and postsynaptic partners and is currently impractical for brain-wide mammalian applications. Similarly, physiological techniques such as channelrhodopsin-assisted circuit mapping (CRACM)12 and Patch-seq15,16 provide precise functional data but are limited by low throughput. Recent sequencing-based strategies (such as Retro-Seq, Project-Seq, VECTOR-Seq, MAPseq and BARseq)17,18,19,20,21 have advanced the field by using RNA barcodes to define projection targets of starter neurons at high throughput, but these strategies trace axonal projection targets in the brain, and do not identify their synaptic target cell types within those areas. Additionally, these methods often rely on tissue microdissection, thereby losing anatomical context. These limitations underscore the need for next-generation, readily adoptable methods for comprehensive connectivity mapping at cell-type resolution.

To fill this gap, with a particular focus on comprehensive mapping of synaptic target cell types, we integrated a genetically encoded anterograde fluorescent trans-neuronal tracer, mWGA–mCherry (mWmC)6, (Fig. 1a) with the spatial transcriptomics technology, MERFISH7,8 (Fig. 1b). This combined platform, which we named TransA-MERFISH, required two major technical advances. First, we established an experimental workflow that enables the combination of anterograde trans-neuronal tracer immunostaining and MERFISH-based spatial transcriptomics. Second, we developed an automated data processing pipeline to align connectivity and transcriptomic data—that is, to overlay fluorescent signals from anterograde tracers on the spatially resolved neural identity data derived from multiplexed RNA signals in MERFISH (Fig. 1c). We then applied TransA-MERFISH to investigate the aforementioned half-century-old unresolved problem in visual neuroscience: the relationship between direction-selective neuron types and computations at different stages of the visual hierarchy. We used TransA-MERFISH to establish a comprehensive, cell-type-resolution wiring diagram downstream of ooDSGCs, a well-studied RGC subclass attuned to stimuli moving in one of the four cardinal directions: nasal, temporal, dorsal or ventral22,23. Using Cre transgenic mice, we mapped the SC synaptic target cell types of ooDSGCs that prefer particular directions24,25,26. We unexpectedly found that although ooDSGCs strongly innervate several SC cell types, they do not innervate the cell type that a previous study27 claimed was most direction-selective in SC. These surprising results were validated using multiple genetic, anatomical and electrophysiological tests. Subsequent in vivo imaging studies of SC activity before and after ablation of retinal direction-selective circuits confirmed that computationally distinct ooDSGC-dependent and ooDSGC-independent direction-selective cell types are commingled in SC. Our research establishes TransA-MERFISH as a high-throughput approach for generating cell-type-level wiring diagrams and reveals divergent computational strategies for visual motion detection.

a–c, Schematic of the TransA-MERFISH workflow. a, AAV2-mWGA-mCherry is delivered to left retina for trans-neuronal transfer of mWmC from all RGCs onto retino-recipient neurons in right SC. b, At 4 weeks post-injection (wpi), sSC was imaged. c, A 140-gene panel was used to classify sSC neurons. Anti-RFP immunostaining was used for mWmC+ cell identification in the MERFISH-segmented atlas. d,e, Uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) plot classifying sSC neurons into 8 ENCs and 11 INCs (d) and with superimposed Slc17a6 (excitatory neurons) and Gad1 (inhibitory neurons) expression (e). f, Median positions of somata along the dorsal–ventral axis for all clusters. Box plots show the median, with the lower and upper bounds of the box representing the 25th and 75th percentiles, respectively. Whiskers indicate the minimum and maximum values. g, Left, dendrogram designating the transcriptomic similarities between clusters. Middle, bar plot showing cluster frequencies. Right, dot plots for sSC marker genes for each ENC or INC. For data in d–g, n = 16 mice, 46,277 cells. h,i, A sample image for segmentation and registration of RNA transcripts (h) and mWmC overlay (i). Colour shades denote cell-mask boundaries generated by Cellpose, and each dot represents a distinct transcript. mWmC+ cells (red neurons) were quantified using a control-derived fluorescence intensity threshold applied to the distribution of red fluorescence intensities (Methods). Scale bars, 200 µm (h) and 25 µm (i). Representative images from five independent experiments with similar results. j, mWmC registration on a sample sSC section. Left, maximum-intensity projection images of DAPI and mWmC overlaid with segmented cell masks in white. Right, Npnt (ENC5 marker) expression overlaid on mWmC registration. Scale bars, 200 µm. ROI, region of interest. k, Bar graphs reporting all retino-recipient neuron clusters. 49.3 ± 3.3% (mean ± s.e.m.) of the sSC neurons are annotated as recipients. n = 3 mice. Data are presented as mean ± s.e.m. *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001; NS, not significant (P ≥ 0.05).

It has been revealed that single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq)-based methods have laid the groundwork for understanding neuronal taxonomy, including scRNA-seq studies covering the entire SC region28,29. However, these methods require tissue dissociation and microfluidics-based single-cell isolation, which reduce spatial resolution, the completeness of cell-type identification, and scalability for large-scale mapping. We therefore developed a preparation to combine anterograde trans-neuronal tracing with spatial transcriptomics (MERFISH). Because the established MERFISH protocol uses fresh-frozen tissue to maximize RNA preservation30,31, it is incompatible with immunostaining for protein markers such as the anterograde trans-neuronal tracer mWmC. Therefore, we developed a protocol to perform MERFISH on fixed tissue. To benchmark this protocol, we sought to create a reference atlas of SC neurons in the retino-recipient superficial SC (sSC) (Fig. 1c). We referred to existing scRNA-seq data6,19,28 to select 140 neuron-type marker genes to classify retino-recipient neurons in the superficial SC (sSC) (Fig. 1b, Extended Data Figs. 1e,f and 2f,i and Methods). We developed a perfusion–fixation MERFISH protocol that ensured that RNA integrity and neuronal morphology were not compromised compared with fresh-frozen tissue, while preserving protein localization (Extended Data Fig. 1a–d and Methods). We then performed MERFISH on sSC, followed by Cellpose-based segmentation (as in past MERFISH studies in the mouse brain31), which covered all sSC neurons (Fig. 1h,i and Methods). This pipeline classified sSC neurons into 8 excitatory cell types (ENC1–8, marked by Slc17a6) and 11 inhibitory cell types (INC1–11, marked by Gad1) (Fig. 1d–g and Extended Data Fig. 1g–j). Data quality for SC cell classification from the modified TransA-MERFISH protocol (Extended Data Fig. 3a–e) closely matched that of several published scRNA-seq datasets19,27,28 (Extended Data Fig. 2c,e–j), as well as the cell types and supertypes reported in the Allen Brain Atlas dataset30 (Extended Data Fig. 2a,b). Together, these data validate the feasibility of performing MERFISH in fixed tissue.

Sources indicate that analysis of spatial distributions found that each ENC cluster is restricted to a specific sublamina along the dorsal–ventral axis (Fig. 1f and Extended Data Fig. 4f), consistent with past observations in rodents and zebrafish6,32,33,34. INC1, INC2, INC5 and INC6 are also restricted to specific sublaminae along the dorsal–ventral axis, whereas INC3, INC4 and INC7–11 are spread across multiple sublaminae (Fig. 1f and Extended Data Fig. 4g). In addition, we observed a consistent distribution of all ENCs and INCs along the anterior–posterior and medial–lateral axes, which largely follows the sublaminar arrangement, without layer swapping (Extended Data Fig. 4a–e). Collectively, the MERFISH data map the sublaminar distribution of sSC neurons along the dorsal–ventral axis at single-cell-type resolution. Each cluster is further compared and quantified in Extended Data Table 1.

In a recent development, having established a MERFISH protocol compatible with immunostaining and created an atlas of sSC cell types, we next sought to overlay cell connectivity information onto it. To do so, adeno-associated virus (AAV) encoding mWmC was delivered to the left eye to yield nearly complete coverage across all RGC types (Fig. 1a and Extended Data Fig. 6a). mWmC protein was transferred anterogradely and monosynaptically to the synaptic targets of RGCs in the contralateral (right) sSC, which receives innervation from around 90% of RGCs35. We then performed MERFISH on fixed tissue followed by anti-RFP immunostaining on the same microscope to facilitate registration with the MERFISH data. As a result, mWmC signals identified by anti-RFP immunostaining could be clearly registered with the RNA-based Cellpose segmentation masks (Fig. 1i,j and Methods). All mWmC+ neurons in the SC downstream of a given RGC starter neuron could be captured by imaging approaches and molecularly identified using MERFISH. Based on co-registered mWmC signals and MERFISH transcripts, we established a computational pipeline to assign mWmC signals to segmented neurons at single-cell resolution, followed by manual proofreading (Fig. 1i,j and Methods). The optimized workflow enabled high-throughput registration. This computational pipeline determines the percentages of mWmC+ neurons within each neuronal cluster, providing a quantitative measure of connectivity at cell-type resolution (Fig. 1k and Methods). We termed this integrated workflow TransA-MERFISH because it combines anterograde trans-neuronal tracing with MERFISH-based cell classification to read out connectivity.

Using TransA-MERFISH, we examined the synaptic target cell types of all RGCs. Roughly half (49 ± 3%, mean ± s.e.m.) of sSC neurons had a detectable mWmC signal (Fig. 1k). Across sSC neuron types defined by MERFISH, 5 out of 8 ENCs and 6 out of 11 INCs were classified as retino-recipient neurons based on mWmC signals above baseline, including a cell type that we recently indicated to be retino-recipient (Npnt+)6 (Figs. 1k and 2a,c and Extended Data Fig. 3f–h). Notably, multiple ENCs and INCs in the sSC did not receive mWmC and were therefore not categorized as recipient neurons of RGCs, including a cell type that was previously6 characterized as not retino-recipient (Etv1+) (Figs. 1k and 2c,o). These data thus suggest TransA-MERFISH possesses the sensitivity and specificity to map synaptic connectivity at scale.

In a recent development, the spatially resolved map of all retino-recipient neurons in SC (Fig. 2b) generated with TransA-MERFISh enabled direct comparison of connectivity across cell types within shared sublaminar contexts. Notably, several SC neuron pairs exhibited divergent RGC connectivity despite occupying similar sublaminar distributions (Figs. 1f and 2a,b,g–o). For example, in the most superficial SC, ENC1 and ENC2 neurons were retino-recipient, whereas neighbouring INC1 neurons were not; similarly, in slightly deeper layers, ENC5 and INC6 neurons received retinal input, whereas neighbouring ENC6 neurons did not. These observations suggested that sublaminar position alone is insufficient to explain synaptic targeting by RGC axons. To test whether molecular cell-type identity contributes to synaptic specificity beyond sublaminar organization, we implemented a permutation-based framework in which cell-type labels were randomly shuffled within depth bins along the dorsal–ventral axis (Fig. 2d and Methods). This procedure preserves the sublaminar distribution of mWmC labelling while disrupting the association between molecular identity and connectivity. Cell-type specificity was quantified by comparing observed mWmC enrichment or depletion for each cell type against the permutation-derived null distribution. Using this approach, we identified multiple retino-recipient clusters, including ENC1, ENC2 and ENC5, with significant enrichment of mWmC labelling after accounting for sublaminar positions (Fig. 2e). By contrast, multiple non-retino-recipient clusters, including INC1 and ENC6, characterized here, indicated significant depletion relative to sublaminar expectations (Fig. 2e,p). Together, these results indicate that RGC axons innervate SC neurons in a cell-type-specific way rather than simply according to their sublaminar distributions; that is, molecular identity, rather than sublaminar distribution, determines wiring specificity from the retina to SC.
