💡 Key Takeaways
  • Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has been provided with a timely team news boost ahead of the Premier League showdown against Manchester United on Sunday.
  • With the international break now concluded, the Reds players who were away with their countries have now reconvened on Merseyside and were put through their paces at the AXA Training Centre on Thursday.
  • There were no fresh injury concerns arising from national team duties, and there had already been good news earlier in the week when Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni resumed first-team training as they both close in on long-awaited returns from lengthy absences.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has been provided with a timely team news boost ahead of the Premier League showdown against Manchester United on Sunday.

With the international break now concluded, the Reds players who were away with their countries have now reconvened on Merseyside and were put through their paces at the AXA Training Centre on Thursday.

There were no fresh injury concerns arising from national team duties, and there had already been good news earlier in the week when Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni resumed first-team training as they both close in on long-awaited returns from lengthy absences.

As per Liverpool Echo, a number of Reds players who had been carrying slight knocks or been absent through injury prior to the international window are now on course to be available for the Man United fixture.

The Dutch trio of Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong all trained, with the captain skipping Netherlands duty due to a minor matter, the midfielder missing our last three games with a heel problem, and the right-back overcoming a muscle injury he sustained in mid-October.

(Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images).

Dominik Szoboszlai had played through a slight knee problem for Hungary in recent days, but he was involved in the session in Kirkby today, albeit with strapping on the affected area.

Two other notable inclusions were Alexis Mac Allister and Ronald Araujo, both of whom partook in training despite being just back from representing their countries in South America, although Bradley and Leoni weren’t involved in today’s session as their recoveries are being managed carefully.

Recent findings suggest that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Iraola will be delighted to get through the international window with no fresh injury absentees (unlike the damaging extended break earlier in the autumn), and also to see those who had been carrying knocks all involved in the session this morning.

The returns of Gravenberch and Frimpong give the head coach greater scope for selection in midfield and at right-back respectively, and Van Dijk and Szoboszlai could both be cleared to start as they seem to have shaken off their minor issues.

Barring any upcoming setbacks between now and Sunday, it looks as though the only definite absentees for the Man United game will be Bradley, Leoni and Hugo Ekitike, each of whom continue to nurse long-term injuries but are on course to return in the coming weeks.

Sources indicate that iraola will inevitably be asked for updates on each of those players when he holds his pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon, and his squad seems to be nicely stocked at the beginning of what’ll be a punishing fixture schedule in the lead-up to the festive period. Long may it stay that way!

Vergara ko, le parole di Maresca e Doku, quelle di Allegri e KDB: la vigilia di Man City-Napoli

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that il Napoli si prepara a una delle trasferte più complicate della propria stagione.
  • Recent findings suggest that il tecnico azzurro non ha nascosto le difficoltà della trasferta inglese: “Giochiamo contro una delle squadre più forti d'Europa”, ha spiegato in conferenza stampa, sottolineando la necessità di una prestazione di grande attenzione collettiva.
  • L'emergenza riguarda soprattutto la difesa.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that il Napoli si prepara a una delle trasferte più complicate della propria stagione. Oggi, martedì 24 novembre, alle ore 21, gli azzurri saranno ospiti del Manchester City all'Etihad Stadium per la quinta giornata della fase a campionato di Champions League. La squadra di Massimiliano Allegri arriva all'appuntamento con appena tre punti conquistati nelle prime quattro partite europee e una lunga lista di indisponibili. Dall'altra parte, però, anche i Citizens attraversano un momento delicato: quattro partite consecutive senza vittorie e un processo di rinnovamento ancora in corso dopo l'addio di Pep Guardiola. Una sfida dal significato particolare soprattutto per Kevin De Bruyne, pronto a ritrovare da avversario lo stadio nel quale ha scritto pagine indimenticabili della propria carriera.

Recent findings suggest that il tecnico azzurro non ha nascosto le difficoltà della trasferta inglese: “Giochiamo contro una delle squadre più forti d'Europa”, ha spiegato in conferenza stampa, sottolineando la necessità di una prestazione di grande attenzione collettiva. “Ci vorrà ottima tecnica quando avremo la palla e quando non ce l'avremo dovremo fare il meglio possibile per creare le condizioni per contrattaccare il Manchester”.

L'emergenza riguarda soprattutto la difesa. Di Lorenzo e Badiashile torneranno disponibili soltanto contro il Lecce, mentre Rafa Marin è squalificato e Favasuli e Marianucci non figurano nella lista UEFA. Tra i 18 convocati ci sono appena quattro difensori di ruolo: Beukema, Olivera, Rrahmani e Spinazzola. Assenti anche Meret e Vergara, con quest'ultimo destinato a uno stop di almeno due mesi per una lesione muscolare di alto grado. La buona notizia è il ritorno di David Neres, nuovamente disponibile dopo oltre un mese. Aggregati anche i giovani Chiummariello e Spinelli.

Allegri ha comunque ribadito che il risultato dell'Etihad non sarà decisivo per il cammino europeo: “L'obiettivo chiaro è passare il turno, indipendentemente da domani”. Sul piano tattico, il tecnico chiede soprattutto di evitare gli errori commessi nella sconfitta contro il Porto, quando la squadra aveva perso compattezza nel tentativo di recuperare il risultato.

Sul fronte inglese, Enzo Maresca ha risposto con una battuta alle parole di Allegri sulla difficoltà della partita: “In Italia siamo abbastanza bravi a piangere. Non ci credo assolutamente”. L'allenatore del City si aspetta infatti un Napoli competitivo: “È una squadra forte, fisica, con giocatori forti. McTominay sta facendo bene, De Bruyne e Hojlund sono top player e c'è Lang che è in forma”.

Maresca ha riconosciuto le difficoltà della propria squadra, ancora alla ricerca di equilibrio dopo i numerosi cambiamenti estivi. Per la partita recupera Matheus Nunes, mentre Semenyo resta indisponibile. Anche Jeremy Doku ha sottolineato la necessità di ritrovare continuità e concretezza sotto porta, spiegando che il gruppo sta ancora assimilando alcune richieste del nuovo allenatore.

Recent findings suggest that il grande protagonista emotivo della vigilia resta però De Bruyne. Il belga ha parlato con affetto della sua ex squadra: “Sono molto fiero di quello che ho fatto come giocatore del City, è il mio club”. Non sono mancati, tuttavia, passaggi delicati sul suo futuro a Napoli e sulle indiscrezioni riguardanti la famiglia. “Ho giocato al 400% fino ad ora. Non ho più 20 anni, ne ho quasi 36, quindi ci sono tante cose da prendere in considerazione”, ha dichiarato, esprimendo anche amarezza per le attenzioni rivolte alla propria vita privata.

According to recent reports, in campo, però, il suo pensiero è rivolto esclusivamente alla sfida: “Noi dobbiamo avere coraggio, non possiamo fare solo lanci lunghi e duelli”. Una convinzione condivisa anche da Allegri, consapevole che per uscire con un risultato positivo dall'Etihad serviranno qualità tecnica, organizzazione e una prestazione di squadra praticamente impeccabile.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:33 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 20 November 2026.

Rangers goalkeeper Ivor Pandur has revealed his 'unbelievable' experience of working under Allan McGregor.

The former Rangers, Hull and Scotland keeper was brought into the Ibrox backroom staff by Derek McInnes as lead goalkeeping coach in the summer.

Pandur is reaping the benefits of his mentor’s experience and their relationship having kept eight clean sheets during his team’s 12-match unbeaten run.

'It’s unbelievable,' noted the Croatian ahead of the Premiership encounter at Motherwell on Saturday night.

'With the career that he had here, he obviously has a lot of experience.

'We have a great relationship where he is my coach, he is my friend. So he’ll tell me when I ask him if I can do something better.

Ivor Pandur has made an impressive start to life at Rangers after joining from Hull City.

'We are here to make each other better. If I can make him a better coach, that’s brilliant. But he’s making me a better goalkeeper and I’m really, really thankful for that.

'Training, first of all, is really, really enjoyable. And he always asks, "What do I want to do? What do I want to improve?". And he’ll give me feedback.

'There’s not a single thing, I would say, that made me better. Just in general, to be able to work in these kind of circumstances and conditions, it’s really enjoyable and it’s making me happy every day.

'It’s making me excited to come to work. And that’s because of him also.

'He’s a great guy and he was a great goalkeeper, and it’s enough for me to learn from.'.

Manager McInnes this week described Pandur as a key 'driver' of team culture off the pitch, citing the respect he has from his team-mates.

Industry observers note that pandur, who joined from Hull in the summer, stated: 'I always want to lead by example. The words are not so important if you’re not doing your job right.

'So if I can lead by example and show up every day, work as hard as I can, a lot of young players can see that.

Pandur insists he is only going to keep improving under the guidance of Allan McGregor.

'And obviously, I’m always there to help somebody. I was also 19 or 20 and, when I had somebody to learn from, it was much easier.

'Because you get experiences through life and through years of playing, I always try to help everybody else.

In a recent development, 'So there are times where I can be more vocal if I feel a need for it, but it’s never my first objective. It’s always to lead by example.'.

Pandur is still awaiting his first international cap but was again away with Croatia this month and he feels meeting the demands of Rangers fans is getting the best out of him.

'It keeps you on your toes,” the former Rijeka, Hellas Verona and Fortuna Sittard player remarked. 'But in my opinion, pressure is in your head.

It has been revealed that 'We all play the game we love and we try to do our best. Some days you’ll do good, some days you’ll do bad. We always try to do the right thing.

'Pressure is bigger here, there’s more followers. But it can only make you better because it gets everything out of you.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Si apre la terza fase per la gara del 13 dicembre; nella vendita libera una persona può acquistare fino a quattro tagliandi.

La vendita libera dei biglietti per Lazio-Roma inizierà martedì 24 novembre alle 11:00. Secondo quanto riportato da Sslazio, Si tratta della terza fase di vendita per il derby, in programma domenica 13 dicembre alle 12:30, come comunicato dalla S.S. Lazio.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Sources indicate that dalle 11:00 del 24 novembre la vendita sarà aperta per tutto lo stadio. Per i posti dell’intera Tribuna Tevere resterà però obbligatorio possedere una fidelity card Eagle Card o Millenovecento. Per procedere online occorrerà inserire il codice della card come coupon; il codice potrà anche essere presentato al momento dell’acquisto.

Sources indicate that ai biglietti acquistati online sarà applicata una commissione di servizio del 3,80%. I possessori di una fidelity card Millenovecento o Eagle che non sono abbonati potranno chiedere, anche acquistando online, che il titolo d’ingresso sia caricato elettronicamente sulla card.

Sources indicate that I biglietti ridotti per invalidi civili al 100% e quelli di Tribuna Tevere per persone non deambulanti, in entrambi i casi con accompagnatore, potranno essere acquistati soltanto nei Lazio Style 1900, escluso il punto vendita di Parco Leonardo. Il ridotto Under 16 è riservato ai ragazzi nati dal 1° gennaio 2010.

Chi compra fisicamente un biglietto in un punto vendita deve mostrare un documento d’identità: senza, il titolo di accesso non può essere emesso, secondo il D.L. 8/2/2010 n. 8. Non sono considerate idonee alla vendita le patenti di ultima generazione che non riportano il luogo di residenza.

It has been revealed that nella vendita libera ogni persona può acquistare al massimo quattro biglietti, secondo le disposizioni dell’Osservatorio sulle Manifestazioni Sportive. Per gli altri tre eventuali intestatari è sufficiente presentare anche una copia del documento d’identità. I bambini di quattro anni nati dal 1° gennaio 2022 entrano gratuitamente e senza biglietto, mostrando un documento d’identità o la tessera sanitaria. All’ingresso l’identità sarà controllata per ogni spettatore: il documento è obbligatorio anche per i minorenni.

#152896. A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control

A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3843 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1,2,3.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1,2,3. Electroceuticals targeting the autonomic nervous system have shown anti-inflammatory effects, yet existing systems lack the metabolic interoceptive feedback to fully restore immune–metabolic homeostasis4,5,6,7,8,9. Here we report an artificial neuroimmune axis (NeuroAxis) as a closed-loop immunomodulatory therapy for treating metabolic diseases. Analogous to its biological counterpart, NeuroAxis is solely powered by endogenous glucose, operating without batteries or wireless power transfer. It emulates the vagal reflex through closed-loop neuromodulation with metabolic interoceptive feedback. In a rat model of type 1 diabetes, NeuroAxis promotes the recovery of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells and reduces inflammatory immune responses; in a rat model of type 2 diabetes, it drives macrophage remodelling and reduces systemic chronic inflammation. In both models, NeuroAxis restores glucose tolerance, improves insulin sensitivity and normalizes glycaemic control, with therapeutic effects persisting after treatment cessation. Our artificial neuroimmune axis promotes substantial advances in treating metabolic disorders and represents a general approach for autonomously regulating interorgan communication, central to homeostasis and pathophysiology.

Missione AEK Atene per il Como: Fabregas predica calma, partita speciale per Douvikas

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, archiviato il successo in campionato contro il Cagliari, il Como si prepara a un altro appuntamento storico.
  • According to recent reports, L'allenatore spagnolo ha innanzitutto elogiato il valore degli avversari: "L'AEK ha messo in difficoltà anche squadre come il Real Madrid.
  • It has been revealed that il tecnico ha poi ribadito la propria filosofia di gioco, prendendo come esempio Massimiliano Alvini: "L'identità viene prima di tutto.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, archiviato il successo in campionato contro il Cagliari, il Como si prepara a un altro appuntamento storico. Domani sera al Sinigaglia arriva l'AEK Atene per la quinta giornata della fase campionato di Champions League, una sfida che potrebbe avvicinare sensibilmente i lariani alla qualificazione. Alla vigilia, Cesc Fabregas e Tasos Douvikas hanno fatto il punto sulle insidie del match e sul momento della squadra.

According to recent reports, L'allenatore spagnolo ha innanzitutto elogiato il valore degli avversari: "L'AEK ha messo in difficoltà anche squadre come il Real Madrid. È una formazione fisica, dominante e con una mentalità importante. Dovremo essere molto efficienti". Nonostante l'entusiasmo attorno al Como, Fabregas invita a mantenere i piedi per terra: "Non siamo favoriti. Siamo una società piccola e sappiamo benissimo quanto possiamo ancora migliorare. Ci siamo guadagnati il rispetto che abbiamo oggi, ma dobbiamo continuare a crescere con calma e gestire le emozioni".

It has been revealed that il tecnico ha poi ribadito la propria filosofia di gioco, prendendo come esempio Massimiliano Alvini: "L'identità viene prima di tutto. Non sei scarso quando perdi e non sei un fenomeno quando vinci. Ci saranno partite da soffrire, ma non cambieremo il nostro modo di giocare". Sul mercato di gennaio, invece, nessuna apertura: "Non è il momento di parlarne, mancano ancora sette partite prima della sosta".

Industry observers note that accanto a Fabregas è intervenuto anche Tasos Douvikas, attuale capocannoniere della Champions League, che vivrà una serata particolare contro un club del suo Paese: "È una cosa bella affrontare una squadra greca. Sarà una partita speciale e molto emozionante", ha spiegato l'attaccante, che ha parlato dell'amicizia con Petros Mantalos: "Non abbiamo ancora parlato della gara, magari ci sentiremo con una videochiamata".

Industry observers note that douvikas ha poi elogiato l'AEK: "È una squadra solida, con qualità e tanta aggressività. Per noi sarà fondamentale il sostegno dei nostri tifosi". Infine, il centravanti ha commentato il primato nella classifica marcatori della competizione: "Essere il capocannoniere è qualcosa di speciale, ma il merito è anche dello staff e dei compagni. Voglio continuare a crescere come calciatore e come persona".

Con un Sinigaglia pronto a spingere il Como verso un'altra notte europea, i lariani cercano un successo che potrebbe rappresentare un altro passo decisivo verso gli ottavi di finale.

Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double

📅 08 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5261 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.
  • According to recent reports, so much for the latest group stage of the competition taking time to warm up.
  • Recent findings suggest that and City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

According to recent reports, so much for the latest group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

Recent findings suggest that and City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

Recent findings suggest that they can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

In a recent development, city will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s.

Sources indicate that there is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a latest City, different personnel and even a new look.

Recent findings suggest that they wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

Sources indicate that the Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

In a recent development, “I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a new team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

Recent findings suggest that phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are new to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

Recent findings suggest that bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

“In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca said. “This highlights how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”.

By Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

Diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he demonstrated why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

In a recent development, city had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

Sources indicate that “It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland said. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the big stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”.

Industry observers note that for Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”.

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS.

Man City have now won seven of their last eight opening matchdays in the UEFA Champions League 🔵Starting strong 💪 pic.twitter.com/CIjsMj4Dig.

“I think we could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. We overall deserved the win and happy with the performance. If you think you can come to a place like this and play and not concede any chances, that is not realistic and it is normal. I am quite lucky as I have a squad of good players. It is a special competition and all the games are very difficult. He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] never panicked and was very good. The performance from him was unbelievable. I am happy to reunite with Enzo [Fernandez], who was very good.”.

Recent findings suggest that 36 - Erling Haaland scored his 36th UEFA Champions League goal for Manchester City, equalling Sergio Agüero as joint-most for the Citizens in the competition.Inevitability. pic.twitter.com/HHbNadybxh.

Industry observers note that “I am so happy with how my teammates have welcomed me into the club. They are not just great players but great human beings. The fans have been absolutely brilliant and this is a upcoming step in my career. Erling [Haaland] is an animal, a beast. Every time I am on the pitch, I will look for him and look to assist him. He is an amazing human being and helped me settle in. I am happy Enzo [Maresca] did all he good to make the move happen. I am so grateful for everything he has done for me and my family.”.

5️⃣9️⃣ appearances 5️⃣9️⃣ goals@Erling's #UCL record 🤯 pic.twitter.com/v6IvpwC9vm.

Sources indicate that “Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a tough game, they play amazing football. We had to deliver on the biggest stage and we did. We controlled the whole of the first half. We created a lot of chances. They pushed us for a good 25 minutes in the second half but we pulled through. These are the games we have to win. We have had a great start to the season.

Industry observers note that “He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] had a really good game and he has been amazing in training. I think we have a gem there. We have to learn and Enzo [Maresca] demands a lot from us. We demand a lot from each other. It was an unreal atmosphere so I hope Enzo is happy with that.”.

The final whistle is blown and Manchester City begin their Champions League campaign with a 2-0 win in Porto. Erling Haaland’s double gives Enzo Maresca a victory in his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City.

Enzo has two shots from range in quick succession, one from a free-kick. The free-kick goes just wide and the second is saved by D Costa.

It has been an ill-tempered game and tempers have boiled over again. Rosario and Haaland are involved in a tussle on the floor, which then leads to a mass melee. Haaland and Rosario are both booked for their part in starting that. Haaland is pleased that he got booked but I am not sure why. Both played their part in that melee.

According to recent reports, enzo Maresca’s side will head home with all three points. Ait-Nouri’s cross from the left side of the box picks out Haaland, who first-time shot from 10 yards out picks out the far corner. A clinical finish from Haaland and Manchester City will start their Champions League campaign with a win.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

There will be five added minutes.

That is really poor refereeing. Porto are denied two clear fouls before Rosario is then punished for a foul on Enzo, which was a foul but so too were the previous two incidents. Francesco Farioli is then booked for his protestations but you can understand their frustration.

Ait-Nouri has the chance to warp up the three points with an effort from the edge of the box but his shot with his weaker right foot goes narrowly wide.

Nothing comes from the corner as Hwang’s delivery to the front post is dreadful.

Haaland has his fourth headed chance of the game but this one goes over the bar from Ndiaye’s cross. Haaland has scored one of those chances but spurned some good ones.

Down the other end, Fofana, only just on, wins Porto a corner and whips up the home fans.

Industry observers note that A final change of the night for Porto sees Fofana replace Veiga. One last roll of the dice from Francisco Farioli.

Sources indicate that whilst Manchester City’s lead is only 1-0, Porto will believe an equaliser is there for them. However, the momentum they were building 10/15 minutes ago has seemingly been lost and the visitors have managed to wrestle back a bit more control.

That is a massive chance missed by Pepe. Gimenez receives it down the left and pings a cross to the back post. The cross perfectly picks out Pepe, who fluffs his lines and completely mis-kicks.

Manchester City are making their final two substitutions of the night as Kovacic and Ait-Nouri come on for Bouaddi and Foden. Ait-Nouri looks like he is going to play left wing.

Two more changes for Porto as Silva and M Fernandes are replaced by Gimenez and Moura.

It has been revealed that porto are going to make their first two changes of the night as Hwang and former Norwich man Sainz come on. Varela and Gomes head off.

In a recent development, for the second time in the half, Donnarumma is lucky. To be fair to the Manchester City keeper, the pass back to him is poor but he is then fortunate. His attempted ball out to his left is intercepted by Gomes but it rolls behind for a goal kick. That ball could have rolled straight into the Manchester City net or fallen straight back at Gomes feet with an empty net ahead of him. Donnarumma was very lucky on Saturday against Coventry to avoid a calamitous moment and he is lucky to avoid another awful moment for the second time in quick succession.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

Sources indicate that ndiaye receives it out on the left before driving inside. He gets his shot away from the edge of the box and tries to pick out the far corner but it is too close to D Costa and an easy save for the Porto keeper.

It has been revealed that A fine pass from Rosario inside his own half cuts through Manchester City’s midfield sends Varela racing through the Manchester City half. He plays it out to his right to find Gomes, who cuts inside onto his left before trying to beat Donnarumma at his near post but the shot goes wide.

Enzo Maresca responds to a shift in momentum in this game making a double change. Anderson and Ndiaye come on for Cherki and Semenyo.

Porto have started to gain some momentum and they want a penalty. Bouaddi is perhaps a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul right on the edge of the box but it may have been just outside the penalty area. You can feel the game starting to turn in Porto’s favour.

It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

It has been revealed that enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Recent findings suggest that manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

It has been revealed that “It is a hard place to come [Porto],” remarked Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that reveals a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”.

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

Industry observers note that “We are going to face one of the major favourites to win the competition,” Farioli noted. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”.

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 15:10 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 15:50 EST, 20 November 2026.

Antonio Conte has claimed clubs are 'frightened of winning' if they have concerns over his methods after the Italian was overlooked for the Manchester United job.

Conte had been heavily linked with the role at Old Trafford, joining Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe and Unai Emery among the list bookmakers' favourites to replace Michael Carrick.

Man United ultimately went with another former Chelsea and Tottenham boss in Mauricio Pochettino, paying around £10million in compensation to lure him away from being head coach of the United States' national team.

Conte, who remains out of work after leaving Napoli in the summer, has now hit back at reports suggesting Man United may have been put off by his intensity and demands.

'First, let me address the question of my method,' Conte told the Cronache di Spogliatoio podcast.

In a recent development, 'If anyone is frightened by my method, then they are frightened of winning, because that methodology leads to victory. That is my answer.

Antonio Conte has claimed clubs are 'frightened of winning' if they have concerns over his methods after the Italian was overlooked for the Manchester United job.

Man United opted to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as head coach after sacking Michael Carrick.

Conte hit back at suggestions Man United's hierachy might have been relucant to appoint him because of his methods.

'Manchester United has such a significant history that I find it strange to imagine anyone could be afraid of an approach aimed at restoring the club to its true stature.

'(United) last won the league in 2013, under Ferguson. I have immense respect for Sir Alex Ferguson.

Sources indicate that 'I've read his book, and when I was in London, I was fortunate enough to visit his home and spend a day with him. He has an incredible passion for talking about football, though, at times, his Scottish accent can be quite hard to follow.

'Through his own methodology and approach, he made Manchester United great.

'That is why I find certain remarks almost offensive toward United; it's as if someone were placing a veto on the club's return to its own history.

Sources indicate that 'A method is what's needed to achieve major results. And if you're suggesting that this method requires hard work, well, yes, it does. Everyone has to work hard, not just the players.'.

Conte has long been known for his combustible personality - as well as an impressive winning record as a coach.

At Chelsea, he fell out with star striker Diego Costa, centre back David Luiz and the club's board. At Napoli, he left a year after winning the Serie A title and said there was 'too much poison, too much malice' at the club.

Conte has developed a reputation for his high intensity and demands, while the Italian famously left Tottenham after an explosive press conference attacking the club's culture.

Conte has won five Serie A titles across three clubs and won the Premier League with Chelsea.

Conte famously left Tottenham after an explosive press conference in 2023, where he labelled his players as 'selfish' and took aim at the club's culture.

The Italian, however, has overseen five Serie A title wins during his spells at Juventus, Inter Milan and Napoli, along with winning the Premier League and FA Cup with Chelsea.

It is not the first time Conte has spoken out in recent weeks following links to Old Trafford, with the 57-year-old having denied he had set 'specific conditions' about taking over at United.

La Repubblica claimed Conte wanted 'carte blanche on the transfer market' and to act as a manager, rather than a head coach, with a technical staff behind the scenes chosen by him involving 'trusted collaborators'.

'My name has been linked with numerous clubs, but there are currently no negotiations at an advanced stage,' Conte responded on social media last month.

Sources indicate that 'Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management. It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right.

In a recent development, 'I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my "strong personality". These reports are unfounded, as there is right now no concrete basis for such assessments.

'Should a concrete opportunity arise, that will be the time to hold discussions with the club concerned and jointly consider the terms of a potential agreement, with due regard for both parties' needs and the qualities and approach that define my work as a manager.'.

Pochettino, who landed the job at Old Trafford, has faced a whirlwind start having flown into Manchester following his final match in charge of the United States on Tuesday.

The Argentine took training for the first time on Thursday and will lead the Red Devils out for the first time on Sunday in a blockbuster clash with Liverpool at Anfield.

Pochettino takes over with Man United lying in the Premier League's relegation zone having won just one of their opening ten matches.

L’ex biancoceleste ricorda l’unica stagione in gialloblù e parla dell’emozione di essere di nuovo in città dopo 26 anni.

Sergio Conceiçao è tornato a Parma per la sfida contro la Roma. In un’intervista a Gianluca Di Marzio ha ricordato il periodo trascorso in gialloblù, dopo l’esperienza alla Lazio, e un gol segnato al Parma da ex con la maglia biancoceleste, dopo il quale esultò poco.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

In a recent development, parma è stata la seconda squadra italiana di Conceiçao, dopo la Lazio. Il suo ritorno gli ha fatto ripensare all’anno trascorso in città: «È un’emozione, un piacere grandissimo tornare qua. Ho vissuto una stagione importante. Sono rimasto solo un anno, ma è stato veramente bello. Mi fa molto piacere ricordare i bei momenti passati qui».

Messo in saccoccia il roboante 5-1 della domenica di campionato ai danni della rivelazione Frosinone, il Milan torna sì a pensare al campo ma inevitabilmente un pensiero lo rivolge anche in direzione del mercato e delle mosse da fare in tal senso, anche quelle che riguardano chi fa già parte del gruppo rossonero.

In a recent development, D'altronde le scorse ore sono state quelle in cui, tra le altre volte, è arrivata la notizia della fumata bianca nelle contrattazioni con l'Eintracht Francoforte per il trasferimento a Casa Milan del dirigente tedesco Markus Krosche, individuato da Cardinale e dai suoi collaboratori come l'uomo giusto per diventare nuovo Head of Football della società rossonera che ha il Diavolo nel suo logo. Come già anticipato da tempo, sarà operativo nelle sue funzioni a partire dal 1° gennaio, ma il suo arrivo sul suolo italiano è atteso prima.

Intanto il fine settimana ha portato in dote un altro gol di Alphadjo Cisse, sempre più sorpresa in positivo dei rossoneri in questo avvio di stagione. Con quello segnato domenica al Frosinone, fanno 9 centri in stagione, dei quali ben 6 in Serie A. Numeri tutt'altro che da riserva e che inducono il club rossonero ad accelerare nelle trattative per il rinnovo, onde evitare inserimenti pericolosi già a gennaio: leggi alla voce Premier League. Stando alle informazioni in nostro possesso, Cisse dovrebbe firmare un contratto fino al 2031 da 1,5 milioni di euro netti a stagione. Il suo entourage sta ragionando sui bonus con il Milan, ma tra le parti si può respirare una certa fiducia nei confronti della chiusura.

Tech Report: The Preview: It's time for Hibs boss Reedijk to bring sunshine back to Leith

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Hibernian supporters know all too well the dangers associated with getting one’s hopes up.
  • It’s a road they’ve been down time and time again, only to end up with that same familiar sickening feeling in the pit of their stomach at the end of it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 16:03 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 16:18 EST, 20 November 2026.

Hibernian supporters know all too well the dangers associated with getting one’s hopes up.

It’s a road they’ve been down time and time again, only to end up with that same familiar sickening feeling in the pit of their stomach at the end of it.

Which is why any talk of the Edinburgh club experiencing some sort of mini-revival should quite rightly be taken with more than a large pinch of salt.

Let’s not forget, at the start of the month, new boss Marink Reedijk had picked up a paltry point from his four games in charge since taking the reins from David Gray.

Performances weren’t up to much either.

A statement win over Hearts at Hampden to book their Premier Sports Cup final spot was backed up with an emphatic 4-0 dismantling of Aberdeen up at Pittodrie.

Hibs manager Marink Reedijk is still searching for his first victory at Easter Road.

According to recent reports, credit where it’s due, of course. Both victories were hard-earned and thoroughly deserved.

It has been revealed that but it’s crucial not to read too much in to either of them. Players going above and beyond in a derby clash should be a given, while the Dons appeared to have chucked it altogether under the stewardship of former manager Stephen Robinson long before Hibs turned up in the Granite City.

The real test begins this weekend with the visit of Dundee United, as Reedijk’s men look to secure a first home Premiership win in over seven months.

The fans have been crying out for entertainment in Leith for far longer than that. In the latter days of Gray’s reign, the atmosphere at Easter Road was verging on toxic.

Reedijk needs to change that, and now has two games against the Dundee clubs over the next four days to get the momentum swinging in the opposite direction.

Continuing to get the best out of his midfield three will be key to that.

The reintroduction of Joe Newell to the starting XI has paid off major-time. Not so much in terms of the stats, but rather what he allows Miguel Chaiwa and Josh Mulligan to do.

The former was linked with a move to Celtic over the summer, but looked miles off it in the early weeks of the campaign until Newell lined up alongside him.

Chaiwa can be guilty of trying to carry out too many jobs in the middle of the park, but Newell’s calming influence has enabled him to stick to what he’s good at — namely breaking up the play and moving the ball on to his more creative team-mates in front of him.

There’s no doubt the Zambian is at his best when he keeps things simple.

Joe Newell has provided a calming influence in the middle of the park amid this upturn in form.

Newell’s presence has also freed Mulligan to play further up the field rather than on the fringes of his own box, where he was popping up far too often a couple of months ago. He’s wasted back there.

If he can add some more goals and assists to his name over the next few, there is every chance he can play himself in to the thoughts of Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli ahead of the next set of internationals.

It should be an intriguing battle this afternoon in the engine room, with United boasting the most cohesive midfield group in the top flight with Dylan Tait, Lyall Cameron and Zidane Iqbal.

Of course, even if Hibs deliver in that sense, it may count for very little if the guys at the top end of the pitch can’t do the business. The lack of cutting edge has been an ongoing concern. Four goals against Aberdeen doesn't change that.

Owen Elding appears to be Reedijk’s preferred option in the central striker role, but while the young Irishman has shown flashes of his potential, he has offered little to suggest he can be relied upon to find the net on a consistent basis.

Industry observers note that the problem is, can anyone? Record-signing Thibault Klidje may have opened his league account for the season against the Dons, however we’ve seen enough to know that he isn’t the answer.

Ante Suto is in the same boat, while Stoke City loanee Nathan Lowe has struggled for both game time and form.

And as for Rabbi Matondo? Well, the wait goes on to see any real return on that investment. Early days, mind you.

That Martin Boyle remains Hibs’ main goalscoring threat is troubling, especially given that the veteran can’t even be considered a nailed-on starter these days.

Industry observers note that there are a significant number of players — across all areas of the park — fighting for their future at the club. Indeed, you would imagine Reedijk is counting down the days until January when he will look to freshen up the squad with guys more suited to his style.

Lyall Cameron has been a key man behind Dundee United's surge up the Premiership table.

Hibs should use today’s opponents as an example of how patience can pay off.

Industry observers note that it’s fair to say that Jim Goodwin has never been Mr. Popular in and around Tannadice. Goodness knows why.

Many fans were calling for his head as recently as the summer after failing to secure a top-six finish last term, but he is slowly but surely starting to win over his doubters.

Make no mistake, this season presents a golden opportunity for United to seriously challenge for third spot.

You never know what you’re going to get from Hearts on any given week, while this is very much uncharted territory for Falkirk.

And let’s face it, nobody would expect the likes of Hibs, Aberdeen or Motherwell to claw themselves into contention.

While everyone else tries to stumble their way through a period of transition, United’s consistency – both on and off the park – could prove to be the difference.

Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

📅 09 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5492 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under upcoming head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.
  • According to recent reports, on the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness.
  • In a recent development, so, earn it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under upcoming head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

According to recent reports, on the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a upcoming contract.

In a recent development, so, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face mentioned it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

According to recent reports, mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W.

There are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he showed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ newly introduced head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

It has been revealed that for Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A big European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola mentioned, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo showed he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

As does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

Recent findings suggest that there was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

It has been revealed that llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc.

We knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

According to recent reports, szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY.

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

Industry observers note that the question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

“I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”.

"You can see he's football mad." ⚽Steven Gerrard on Andoni Iraola's passion and the impact he's making at Liverpool 👏🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M3qKhxt8HE.

Sources indicate that andoni Iraola has been speaking to TNT Sports and has confirmed that it was just cramp for the likes of Bradley Barcola, rather than an injury. Milos Kerkez also went off late with what appears to be just cramp.

Atletico had more possession in the second half but Liverpool were much the better side after the break.

"We can achieve everything we want." 💪Dominik Szoboszlai full of belief after Liverpool's Champions League victory over Atletico Madrid 👀🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ebSvagW4yx.

There is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool start their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid. Liverpool did fall behind to Marcos Llorente’s goal but goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister give Andoni Iraola a win in his first Champions League game as a manager.

Victory in MD1 🤩 #UCL pic.twitter.com/SWFFhSudFJ.

According to recent reports, first Champions League game. First Champions League win for Andoni Iraola ✅ pic.twitter.com/D3CE6w6V0b.

Koumas is tripped by Le Normand and that should be it.

That is a silly foul from Lookman, with Frimpong inside his own box running back towards his own goal, but Lookman decides to push him in the back.

Just 60 seconds remain at Anfield.

There will be five added minutes.

Sources indicate that liverpool think they have sealed it through Frimpong but the offside flag has gone up. First Munoz cuts onto his right and has a shot saved by Oblak. The ball falls to Frimpong, who slots home but he was clearly offside when Munoz took the initial shot.

Recent findings suggest that kerkez is currently down with cramp and his night is done. He will be replaced by Tsimikas and Liverpool will make their final change at the same time. Koumas comes on for Isak.

Atletico win a corner but it all stems from sloppy play in the centre of the pitch from Gravenberch. He has had a few sloppy moments since coming on.

The corner is flicked on by Hjulmand but ends up coming to nothing.

It has been revealed that it isn’t the headline making performance, by any means, but that shouldn’t dilute the importance of Ronald Araujo’s contribution for Liverpool tonight and, indeed, against Ipswich last Friday. He’s doing what Liverpool wanted him to, providing versatility and leadership in their back four and - more than anything - quality. He hasn’t put a foot wrong.

Sources indicate that atletico win a corner out on the left in front of their travelling supporters. Grimaldo’s outswinger is flicked on by the head of Hancko at the near post but it goes over.

Isak has the chance to potentially seal the victory for Liverpool but Le Normand makes a crucial block. Le Normand has only just come on but already made a couple of defensive actions.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool win a corner out on the left with the last touch coming off Pubill, who was marking Van Dijk from a free-kick. Szoboszlai’s inswinger is headed away by Le Normand.

Digeo Simeone is making his final two substitutions of the night as Le Normand and Hjulmad replace Romero and Barrios,.

Atletico bring on David, on loan from Juventus, for Baena.

Recent findings suggest that alvarez has a chance inside the Liverpool box but his shot is straight at Alisson. There are some appeals for handball but it hit Munoz from such close range that it is never a penalty.

Liverpool are making a substitution as Mac Allister, who scored the goal to put Liverpool in front, is replaced by Gravenberch. Mac Allister, who made some comments in the press conference yesterday about his sadness at not being offered a upcoming contract, put in a good performance in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield. He was on a booking though so probably sensible to take him off when you can guarantee that the Atletico players would have tried to get him sent off.

We’ll see what happens in the coming weeks and months but there have been glimmers here with Florian Wirtz looking better than he has done with pace to pass to; if it clicks with him, Bradley Barcola & Alexander Isak it could be exciting but one game must be built on. It’s frustrating that Barcola’s night has ended with what appears to be cramp or tightness in his calf because he was getting more joy than he had done before half-time. The significant challenge for Liverpool, too, is whether they have the nous to see this contest out.

The new Netherlands boss Xavi is in attendance at Anfield tonight, watching the likes of Van Dijk, Frimpong and Gravenberch, although the latter is still yet to come off the Liverpool bench.

This is a concern for Liverpool. Barcola has gone down and seems to have some pain in his left calf. Is it cramp or an injury? It will be a double change for the home side as Frimpong and Munoz come on. Barcola is given a standing ovation as he goes off and the Liverpool fans will be hoping it is just cramp. Ngumoha also heads off.

Sources indicate that liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

According to recent reports, andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a major challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

Recent findings suggest that “It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a big responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”.

Recent findings suggest that atletico Madrid right now sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone stated. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”.

Recent findings suggest that il penultimo di novembre 2026 potrebbe passare alla storia recente come il lunedì nero degli infortuni in Serie A. Dopo il fine settimana del campionato, per molte società è arrivato il conto e in alcuni casi anche piuttosto salato, visto che c'è tra gli altri anche chi rischia di aver finito qui la sua stagione.

In a recent development, la lista di chi dovrà fermarsi ai box fa paura e induce probabilmente anche a qualche riflessione di carattere più generale, visto che mai come quest'anno (a numeri) i protagonisti della Serie A devono fare i conti con gli infortuni. Finita per esempio la stagione di Lorenzo Colombo: lesione al legamento crociato per il centravanti del Genoa. Si rivedrà solo nel 2027 anche Marco Carnesecchi: il portiere dell'Atalanta nelle prossime ore sarà operato al menisco mediale. Appuntamento a primavera per Antonio Vergara: il centrocampista del Napoli ha rimediato una lesione di alto grado al bicipite femorale e dovrà fermarsi per mesi.

Non finisce qui, però: qualche problemino, per esempio, ce l'ha anche la Juventus. Diretto, come il sovraccarico alla coscia che impensierisce Kerim Alajbegovic (non giocherà giovedì in Europa League ma non dovrebbe essere nulla di grave) o in prospettiva, come nel caso di Vasilije Adzic: il centrocampista, in prestito al Sassuolo, si è sottoposto a visite più approfondire per determinare l'entità dell'infortunio al ginocchio che lo tormenta. Finita qui? Macché, perché in casa Roma ha alzato bandiera bianca di nuovo Devyne Rensch: problema al flessore per l'olandese, che sarà presto rivalutato. E poi i guai del Torino, che ha perso Ardian Ismajli (distrazione di basso grado agli adduttori più frattura alla mano, almeno tre partite fuori) e deve fare i conti pure con l'infiammazione al ginocchio di Rafik Belghali.

It has been revealed that ultimo, ma non ultimo, Endrick. Il brasiliano da diverse settimane è nel mirino di Milan e Roma per gennaio e anche lui è rimasto vittima di un infortunio: lesione all'adduttore per il brasiliano, da definire nei dettagli.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il tennista sarà operato a Turku il 24 novembre; le prime stime indicano un recupero di circa tre-quattro mesi.

Jannik Sinner ha deciso di sottoporsi a un intervento al ginocchio destro. L’operazione è programmata per martedì 24 novembre a Turku, in Finlandia, e sarà eseguita dal professor Lasse Lempainen. La scelta arriva dopo diversi consulti medici e oltre quattro mesi di terapie conservative che non hanno dato i risultati sperati.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Industry observers note that le prime stime indicano un recupero di circa tre-quattro mesi. Il rientro potrebbe avvenire in primavera, ma i tempi dipenderanno dall’esito dell’intervento e dalla successiva riabilitazione.

Il 12 luglio Sinner aveva conquistato il suo secondo Wimbledon consecutivo battendo Alexander Zverev in finale. Quella partita è stata anche la sua ultima apparizione ufficiale della stagione. Nelle settimane successive il tennista italiano ha cominciato ad avvertire dolore al ginocchio destro.

Il problema è stato identificato come una sindrome della bandelletta ileotibiale, che provoca dolore nella parte esterna dell’articolazione. Per un atleta sottoposto a sollecitazioni continue può diventare particolarmente fastidiosa.

All’inizio Sinner e il suo gruppo di lavoro avevano scelto di evitare la chirurgia. Il percorso prevedeva riposo, fisioterapia e trattamenti specifici, con l’obiettivo di recuperare gradualmente la piena funzionalità del ginocchio senza correre rischi inutili o compromettere ulteriormente la carriera del tennista.

In a recent development, nonostante i tentativi e i consulti con diversi specialisti, il dolore non è scomparso definitivamente. Il numero due del mondo ha quindi preso in considerazione l’intervento. Decisivo è stato l’ultimo confronto con Lempainen, chirurgo ortopedico finlandese specializzato nel trattamento delle lesioni muscolari e tendinee degli sportivi professionisti.

Tra gli atleti già seguiti dal medico figurano anche i calciatori Ousmane Dembélé e Leonardo Spinazzola. Dopo la valutazione della situazione clinica di Sinner, la scelta è ricaduta sull’operazione a Turku.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By IAN LADYMAN, FOOTBALL EDITOR.

Published: 16:51 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:07 EST, 20 November 2026.

In a soft-focus Sky TV interview that followed Mauricio Pochettino’s opening press conference on Friday, the Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada revealed there had been a ‘buzz’ about the club since the arrival of their newly introduced manager.

Whether he was speaking metaphorically or referring to the sound of drones stealing Pochettino’s training secrets from above only he will know.

As is usually the case these days, much about the modern United remains unclear.

But what we do know after welcoming the eighth full-time manager since the days of Sir Alex Ferguson is that once again England’s biggest football club is relying on a personality lift to drag them back to their feet.

This is what happens when you get things wrong for so long, when you buy the wrong players and install executives who appear to be learning on the job. You end up hiring and firing managers, waiting for the one who finally arrives with the magic dust, the capacity to somehow create something greater than the sum of the rather wonky parts.

Listening to Pochettino here – a talented coach and a good person – was to occasionally think back to words spoken in the weeks of their arrivals on this territory by predecessors such as Ruben Amorim and Erik ten Hag.

In a recent development, for they too were asked about such intangibles as culture and mood and philosophy. They too were asked about more prosaic football matters such as match fitness.

It’s a conversational cycle that tells a story of recurring and systematic football failure.

Mauricio Pochettino faced reporters in his first press conference as Manchester United boss on Friday.

A drone captured footage of Pochettino's first training session on Thursday.

Amorim – back on a grim, foggy day exactly two years ago – was asked about Marcus Rashford and whether he had been right to spend time off in Upcoming York days before the new United manager walked through the door.

Here, Pochettino could justifiably have been asked about another forward Bryan Mbeumo spending the wee hours of Thursday morning playing the newly released Grand Theft Auto video game when he probably should have been asleep.

This is the United that Pochettino is now being asked to fix, a club where names and faces change but problems remain the same.

The Berrada interview was actually more enlightening than Pochettino’s carefully managed introduction to the wider media.

Sources indicate that certainly it was interesting to listen to his assertion that nine defensive players in one squad was enough. In football, as United are discovering yet again, it’s not necessarily the quantity that matters but the quality.

One point did resonate rather more deeply, though, and that was the one Berrada – once of Manchester City – made about United’s players needing a manager capable of dealing with the scrutiny of the club and who could shield some of his players from all that comes with it.

The recently-departed Michael Carrick did look rather lost on the touchline in the final tumultuous weeks of his time as manager. He didn’t look an awful lot more comfortable in front of the TV cameras either.

Bryan Mbeumo posted this picture after the midnight release of Grand Theft Auto VI.

In the dressing room? Well, he lost the loyalty of his captain Bruno Fernandes towards the end and that is never a good sign.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino will do rather better at all that. The former Chelsea, PSG and Tottenham manager has a personality and a charisma that could fill an aircraft hangar. His players will arrive at Anfield for his opening game on Sunday feeling better about themselves than they have for some time.

United have hired some confidence and some authority and some experience at a time when they desperately need it, even if Berrada’s claim that they had to call the USA Federation last week to check on his release clause suggested this is an appointment made rather on the hoof.

Recent findings suggest that it is, however, the impact that Pochettino can bring over time on a jumbled squad put together for six different managers over an incredible 12 years that will define him. Here, the 54-year-old undoubtedly faces challenges.

Talking this week to someone associated with Tottenham about Pochettino’s progressive seasons there between 2014 and 2019, I was reminded of the quality that the Argentinian was given to work with.

Pochettino's Spurs side harnessed the attacking power of stars including Harry Kane and Heung-min Son.

The French international goalkeeper, Hugo Lloris, the Belgian central defensive partnership of Toby Alderweireld and Jan Vertonghen, England international defenders Kyle Walker, Danny Rose and Kieran Trippier and, further forward, the burgeoning attacking talents of Dele Alli, Christian Eriksen, Heung-min Son and Harry Kane.

Sources indicate that it was a prototype Premier League football team, both in talent, age, fitness and physicality. That was why, in 2016, it almost won it.

Pochettino does not have this at Old Trafford. He doesn’t have anything like it. He has some talented players. The fact he inherits a team in the bottom three is down to Carrick’s inadequacies.

But this United squad is a mish-mash and it serves a purpose to ask how many would get in that old Spurs team we talk about.

Fernandes? Maybe. Mbeumo? Probably. That is about it and that, frankly, is where United are right now.

Industry observers note that pochettino has long wanted this job. It’s not a posting of convenience for him. Like others before him – men like Jose Mourinho and Louis van Gaal – he has long since coveted the cachet, the stature and the power of this remarkable football institution.

Mourinho and Van Gaal had better players than Pochettino is being handed and they both still failed, largely because they were shown to be coaches already over the top of that hill that both had worked so desperately hard to climb.

Mbeumo is one of the few United players who might have got into Pochettino's Spurs side.

Sources indicate that where does Pochettino sit in terms of his own personal and professional growth? That is such a hard question to answer and will be utterly fundamental to how he travels in the weeks and months to come.

Sitting here fresh from the training ground and strangely seeming to question whether the glass of water in front of him was fit to drink, Pochettino declared himself to be in his coaching prime.

‘I am a much better coach now,’ he mentioned.

The proof or otherwise of that will only be revealed out on the grass. For all that he can plead valid mitigation, Pochettino was not hugely impressive in Paris or at Stamford Bridge. Before he starts to talk about dysfunctional football clubs, he may wish to take a look at his upcoming surroundings.

It has been revealed that liverpool away feels like something of a free hit. Sporting in Lisbon on Wednesday less so and Brentford at home next Saturday definitely not. And so it begins. A run of 12 games in six and a half weeks that may well see Pochettino crawling into January begging for fresh legs and new players.

The newly introduced manager said here that he wishes to be across transfers and little wonder. When he looks at the mistakes made in that regard by a succession of United regimes and executives, he may indeed question what it is they put in the water in the north-west.

United fans will perhaps appreciate that one of the ‘higher ups’ at Old Trafford has finally put his head above the parapet, even if they question some of what Berrada said. That’s been overdue.

Recent findings suggest that in terms of their upcoming manager, they can be forgiven for keeping a lid on any excitement. Many of them have simply been wearied by the cycle.
